Definition: a pomegranate, the tree (from its upright growth) or the fruit (also an artificial ornament)
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses rimmôwn for a pomegranate, the tree (from its upright growth) or the fruit (also an artificial ornament). It stands in 1 Kings 7:18, "…made the pillars, and two rows round about…", and in 1 Samuel 14:2, "…Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rimmôwn is worth knowing, because nothing in Scripture is there by accident.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
